vocabulary.meaning: a way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way
using words to express the opposite of what is meant
the use of irony to mock or show contempt
an imitation of a style or work for comic effect
making something seem less important than it is
making something seem more important than it is
the ability to use words cleverly and humorously
making fun of someone or something
an indirect remark, often suggesting something bad
to publicly criticize using ridicule or irony

grammar_tips.title: Subjunctive Mood for Hypotheticals
grammar_tips.explanation: Satire and irony often use 'if I were' to create hypothetical situations. Example: If I were king, I’d ban all work on Mondays.

grammar_tips.title: Contrast with Connectors
grammar_tips.explanation: Words like 'but', 'however', and 'yet' signal irony or contrast. Example: He said he was thrilled, yet his face was blank.

example_sentences.sentence: The cartoon used satire to highlight political issues.
Her use of irony made the story more entertaining.
He said, 'Great job!' after I dropped the plate, using sarcasm.
The film is a parody of classic detective movies.
He described the storm as 'a bit of rain', an example of understatement.

vocabulary.question: Which word means 'criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way'?
The use of ___ can make a story more entertaining by expressing the opposite of what is meant.

sentence.question: He used ___ to make fun of the politician’s speech.
